title: the newly stated priority ordering is not an agent or gate contract

human_turns.quote: First cirlcle looks good. More of a question, no action needed at this stage. Why is the window launching at roughly 1/9th of the size of the 4k monitor screen. And when resizing, I notice the bounds you have drawn in the map is about 1/4 of the screen. are we using default window size? and is that the right intent for the map size?

body:
_Occurrences: one independent human statement, S20:H6; the same statement is recorded in `slice-13-renderer-performance.md`._

S20:H6 sets the standing order explicitly: performance first, code maintainability second, distribution size third, each at least as important as prompt fidelity, and says it “cannot drop.” The existing `godot-performance-evidence` skill only requires measurement before optimisation; the gate stages documented in `docs/GATE.md` contain no runtime-performance or distribution-size check, and no session prompt or proposal field records this ordering. This is therefore a high-priority standing preference, but only one independent occurrence; it should not be presented as a repeated correction yet.

**Proposed kit/process change** — add an immutable priority block to every game-builder session prompt and require each proposal to record its performance, maintainability, distribution-size, and prompt-fidelity impacts/trade-offs. Add report-only budget fields for runtime measurements and exported-size measurements so a slice cannot claim success without saying which priorities were measured. Keep the human approval decision intact; this is a prompt/schema/process contract, not a game-code rule.

**Confidence** — medium for recurrence, high for the preference itself: the human stated it unambiguously and explicitly asked that retrospectives preserve it, but there is one independent occurrence.
**Cost** — medium: prompt/template, proposal schema, renderer, and validation/test fixtures; higher if size budgets become blocking.
**Mechanically checkable** — partly. Presence, ordering, required fields, and numeric evidence are checkable; whether an agent genuinely made the trade-off correctly still requires human review.
